2609.06807.title: Comparative Study of Anatomical and Learned Features in AI Models for Structural Brain MRI
2609.06807.paper_summary: In this work, we comprehensively evaluate three popular feature-extraction paradigms in AI-based neuroimaging modeling: (1) computation of anatomical surfaces and volumes, (2) supervised learning with convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and (3) unsupervised pretraining of vision transformer (ViT) foundation models, followed by supervised finetuning. Our study is based on 18 publicly available datasets containing 3D structural T1-weighted MRI scans from approximately 80,000 participants across seven distinct clinical tasks. We observe that a linear model based on anatomical features matches the diagnostic performance of complex nonlinear features learned by sophisticated AI frameworks, including foundation models trained on thousands of scans. Conversely, CNNs and pretrained ViTs learn features that implicitly capture relevant anatomical information, bypassing the need for explicit feature extraction. Building upon these insights, we propose Anatomy Segmentation Pretraining (ASP), a novel method to incorporate anatomical information during foundation-model pretraining, which outperforms existing models in biological age estimation.
2609.06807.paper_summary_zh: 在這項研究中，我們全面評估了三種基於人工智慧的神經影像建模中流行的特徵提取範式：(1) 解剖表面和體積的計算，(2) 使用卷積神經網絡 (CNN) 的監督學習，以及 (3) 視覺轉換器 (ViT) 基礎模型的無監督預訓練，隨後進行監督微調。我們的研究基於18個公開可用的數據集，這些數據集包含來自約80,000名參與者的3D結構T1加權MRI掃描，涵蓋七個不同的臨床任務。我們觀察到，基於解剖特徵的線性模型在診斷性能上與由複雜的非線性特徵學習的高級AI框架（包括在數千個掃描上訓練的基礎模型）相匹配。相反，CNN和預訓練的ViT學習的特徵隱式捕捉相關的解剖信息，無需明確的特徵提取。在這些見解的基礎上，我們提出了解剖分割預訓練 (ASP)，這是一種在基礎模型預訓練過程中納入解剖信息的新方法，並且在生物年齡估計上超越了現有模型。
